blocks.text:
# Factory Board v3 (site/factory)

Real-time-ish board for the SM machine: three factories side by side (tabs),
cards flowing through the full label pipeline — development → PR → review →
approved queue → validating → merged — with lifecycle timestamps, a mini
SVG timeline per card, readable per-lane progress, a details drawer
(state history + timings + token spend), and the issue backlog lanes.
Zero build, zero tokens, zero rate limits: the data is a JSON snapshot
each factory's SM tick publishes to its repo's `factory-data` branch
(raw.githubusercontent CDN link).

## Data flow

```
SM tick (sm_github.json, per factory repo)
  └─ end of pass: buildFactoryState() + publishFactoryState()
       └─ gh api PUT repos/O/R/contents/data/<asset>   (factory-data branch)
            └─ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/O/R/factory-data/data/<asset>
                 └─ board fetch() every refreshMs (schema 1 + 2 both render)
```

Factories on the board today:

| tab | repo | asset | state-publish |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| flutter_agent_harness | IstiN/flutter_agent_harness | `fa-state.json` | on |
| dmtools-dart | epam/dmtools-dart | `dart-state.json` | on |
| dmtools-agents | IstiN/dmtools-agents | `agents-state.json` | on |

## Deploy (any static host)

1. Copy this folder.
2. Edit `config.js` — factories[] (stateUrl, accent), lanes,
   backlogColumns, badgeLabels.
3. Style: only `:root` variables in `styles.css` (+ `data-theme="light"`
   overrides). Design tokens mirror `site/index.html` (slate palette,
   JetBrains Mono — embedded, no CDN). Embeddable via `?theme=light|dark`.

## Enable publishing for a factory (OPT-IN)

The machine workflow passes `state-publish` (JSON string) to factory-sm.yml:

```yaml
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
```

- `channel: 'release'` — the only channel today; anything else = off.
- `repo` — target repo (default: the tick's repo).
- `tag` — the data branch name (default `factory-data`; all three factories
  use it — the board URLs share the shape).
- `asset` — one asset per factory (`fa-state.json`, `dart-state.json`,
  `agents-state.json`).

## State schema (v2)

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "factory": "flutter_agent_harness",
  "repo": "IstiN/flutter_agent_harness",
  "tick": { "at": "...", "dryRun": false, "processed": ["pr-817"] },
  "checks": ["Quality gate", "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)", "Binaries smoke gate"],
  "lanes": {
    "development":   [ { "issue": 315, "title": "...", "labels": ["agent:dev"],
                         "url": "https://github.com/O/R/issues/315",
                         "devStartedAt": "..." } ],
    "pr_created":    [ { "pr": 870, "title": "...", "labels": [],
                         "prCreated": "...", "checks": null } ],
    "review":        [ { "pr": 860, "labels": ["ai_pr_reviewed"],
                         "prCreated": "...", "reviewedAt": "..." } ],
    "approved_queue":[ { "pr": 828, "queuePos": 1, "approvedAt": "..." } ],
    "validating":    [ { "pr": 817, "checks": { "verdict": "in_progress",
                         "at": "...", "url": "..." }, "validatingAt": "..." } ],
    "merged_recent": [ { "pr": 801, "mergedAt": "...", "approvedAt": "...",
                         "validatingAt": "..." } ]
  },
  "counts": { "development": 1, "pr_created": 1, "review": 1,
              "approved_queue": 1, "validating": 1, "merged_recent": 1 }
}
```

Lanes are a deterministic read of the machine labels (the same predicates
the reconcile rules query), in PIPELINE order: `agent:dev` (no
`ai_developed`) → development; open, no machine labels → pr_created;
`ai_pr_reviewed` → review; `pr_approved` → approved_queue (FIFO by PR
number, `queuePos` 1-based); `ai_validating` → validating (mutex); merged
within 24h → merged_recent.

Timestamps on every card (the v2 feature — the pipeline becomes measurable):

- `prCreated` / `mergedAt` — GitHub fields (`created_at` / `merged_at`),
  exact from the first snapshot.
- `reviewedAt` / `approvedAt` / `validatingAt` / `devStartedAt` — label
  transition times, accumulated tick-over-tick: the tick fetches the
  previous snapshot off the `factory-data` branch (one `gh api` call),
  carries forward what it stamped before, and stamps `now` on transitions
  it witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). Exact
  to the tick cadence (~10 min). First snapshot after the upgrade: these
  stay `null` until each card's next transition — honest unknowns, and the
  per-tick `<base>-history.json` snapshots keep the raw evidence.

The board renders schema 1 snapshots too (`fresh` maps onto `pr_created`,
timestamp chips simply don't render) — old history files never break it.

## v3 additions (owner 2026-10-03 — additive, schema stays 2)

Old snapshots render untouched; every new key is optional.

### `card.history` — state timeline (details drawer + timings)

Every card may carry `history: [{state, at}]` (oldest first), accumulated
tick-over-tick by the same mechanism as the v2 timestamps: carried
forward, appended when the tick witnesses a transition, capped at 24
entries. PR states are lane ids; issue states are backlog bucket ids.
The first entry after the upgrade carries no `at` (honest unknown). The
board falls back to deriving a timeline from the v2 timestamp fields when
`history` is absent, so pre-v3 snapshots still get a usable drawer.

### `backlog` — issues as board lanes

```json
"backlog": {
  "in_dev":  [ { "issue": 402, "title": "...", "assignee": "ai-teammate",
                 "labels": ["agent:dev"], "url": "...", "bucket": "in_dev",
                 "history": [...], "devStartedAt": "..." } ],
  "queued":  [], "blocked": [], "inbox": []
},
"backlogCounts": { "in_dev": 1, "queued": 0, "blocked": 0, "inbox": 0 }
```

Fed by ONE search call per tick (`repo:X is:issue is:open`). Bucketing is
a deterministic read of the machine's own signals, first match wins:

| bucket | signal |
| --- | --- |
| `blocked` | the `blocked` label — owner hold, its own visually distinct column |
| `in_dev` | assigned to the machine author (the `machineAuthor` deployment knob — a comma-separated login list, gh-728; unconfigured → no assignment bucketing at all) |
| `queued` | `agent:dev` label, not assigned |
| `inbox` | everything else (no label/assignee) |

**Page limit**: the search tool returns a single page (no `perPage` knob),
so a repo with more open issues than one page truncates at the source. Each
bucket is additionally capped at `BACKLOG_CAP` (50, newest kept) in
`js/factoryState.js` — the published snapshot stays bounded, and
`backlogCounts` always equal what the snapshot actually holds (a truncated
lane never masquerades as an empty one). A deployment with more issues than
that should narrow the query instead.

Issues carrying `ai_developed` have handed off to the PR side — they leave
the backlog (unless blocked). Backlog issues share one history array with
their development-lane twin, so the drawer tells the same story from both.

### `card.tokens` — OPTIONAL per-leg token spend

```json
"tokens": [ { "leg": "story_development", "at": "...", "prompt": 48210,
              "completion": 12980, "total": 61190 } ]
```

Keyed `pr-N` / `issue-N` in the builder's `tokens` input. Factories whose
legs report usage (fa's bench) drop a keyed JSON file into the tick's
checkout — `statePublish.tokensFile`, default
`outputs/token_usage/factory_tokens.json`; `readTokensFile()` picks it up
(or returns null on ANY miss — the tick never fails over tokens).
Factories that don't report tokens yet publish token-less cards and the
drawer renders `tokens — not reported by this factory`. The schema never
requires the key.

### Board surfaces

- **Lane summaries** — `N total · M done · K in-flight · Q queued` (+
  blocked) per lane, with a thin segmented progress bar (done / in-flight /
  queued / blocked). Done = merged; in-flight = dev leg running or mutex
  validating; queued = waiting on the next machine step; blocked = owner
  hold. Cards and timeline dots stay as decoration.
- **Details drawer** — click any PR/issue card: header (number, title,
  head sha, current state, labels, `open o…

For the board: hiding when nothing priced avoids a confusing "$0.00" on factories where the pricing table exists but models don't match (e.g. pre-fa#1460 — models all empty → nothing priced → don't show $0.00). That's actually important: pre-fa#1460, ALL rows have model:null → pricedLegs 0 → showing "Σ$0.00" would be misleading ("everything free?"). So: publish `costs` only when pricedLegs > 0. That's what my test demands and it's the right call. Implementation: in buildFactoryState, `if (costs && costs.pricedLegs > 0) state.costs = costs;` — or in priceTokens return null when pricedLegs===0? No — keep priceTokens returning the summary (pure), gate at the snapshot attach. Hmm — but the "Σ$ rounds to cents" test expects usd14d=0.18 > 0 fine. And "undated rows" test: `st.costs.usd14d` = 0 with pricedLegs 0 — WAIT that test does `assert.equal(st.costs.usd14d, 0)` — it EXPECTS st.costs to exist with usd14d 0! Conflict!

Let me re-read my undated test:
```js
test('undated rows still price per-row but stay out of the Σ$ window (honest unknown)', ...
    assert.equal(cardFor(st, 31).tokens[0].cost, 3);
    assert.equal(st.costs.usd14d, 0);

```
Here pricedLegs=0 (undated → out of window) but I expect st.costs to EXIST with usd14d=0. Hmm — inconsistent with the "unknown model → no costs" test? In the undated case the model IS known and priced — the ledger HAS priced spend, it's just not placeable in the window. So showing "Σ$0.00 · 14d · 0 priced legs" would... hmm. Actually what should the header show there? The rows are priced ($3 per row visible on cards) but the 14d rollup can't count them (no dates) → header Σ$ = 0.00. Is showing "Σ$0.00" while a card shows "$3.00" contradictory? A tooltip could explain... This is getting too subtle. Let me simplify to a coherent rule:

**Rule: the snapshot carries `costs` iff pricing is loaded AND at least one row priced (cost attached).** usd14d = Σ in-window; pricedLegs = rows priced in-window.

- unknown model only → no rows priced → no costs. ✔ (test 2)
- absent model only → no costs. ✔ (test 3)
- undated rows priced → rows priced (>0) → costs EXISTS, usd14d=0, pricedLegs=0. ✔ (test 4 — header shows $0.00; per-row $ shows on cards; acceptable, honest: the rollup window can't place them)

Hmm wait, but is that inconsistent-looking? pricedLegs means "in-window priced legs" — undated priced rows aren't counted. The header tooltip says "N priced legs (14d)". It's coherent: the costs block is the 14d-window rollup; its zeros mean "nothing in the window". The GATE for showing the block is "pricing produced at least one $ anywhere" — i.e., pricing is live and matching. OK.

So implementation: `if (costs && (costs.pricedLegs > 0 || ...))` — hmm, undated case: pricedLegs=0 but a row HAS cost. Gate should be "any row priced". Let me track that separately: `summary.priced = true` when any row gets cost? Or count total priced rows regardless of window: add `pricedRows` (all) vs `pricedLegs` (in-window)? Simpler: gate on "any cost attached" via a private flag. Hmm — but flag in summary leaks to snapshot. Use a local var in priceTokens:

```js
var any = false;
... row.cost = cost; any = true;
...
if (!any) return null;
return summary;
```
Wait — but then priceTokens returns null when no rows priced — and buildFactoryState `if (costs) state.costs = costs` suffices. And the undated test: any=true → costs exists, usd14d 0, pricedLegs 0 ✔. Unknown-model test: any=false → null → no costs ✔. Clean. And priceTokens pure semantics: null = "nothing priced".

NO...')` — my own test comment is confusing; I wrote the assertion then contradicted it in the message and then asserted cost===3. For the ABSENT model test: `assert.notOk('cost' in cardFor(st, 31).tokens[0])` got true — cost attached to a model-less row?! Why? ratesFor(pricing, null)... let me re-check ratesFor:

```js
function ratesFor(pricing, model) {

```
model null → return null. priceTokens: `if (!row || row.model == null) return;` — skips before ratesFor. So cost shouldn't attach... unless the failure is from a DIFFERENT assertion in that test. The message "expected falsy, got: true" — could be `assert.notOk('costs' in st)` → 'costs' in st is true — because priceTokens returns a summary whenever pricing is set (the bug identified above, failure mode #2). Yes! Same root cause. OK.

- Test: multi-key → drop the stray notOk line.
- Impl: priceTokens returns null when no row was priced (gate via `any`).

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# Regenerate the factory board visual-check fixtures (site/factory/visual-check/).
#
# The board is zero-build and reads live `factory-data` snapshots; these
# fixtures are captured against the BUNDLED fixture snapshot instead
# (visual-check/fixture.json, via the board's ?fixture= mode) so every
# surface — lane summaries, progress bars, backlog lanes, details drawer,
# token table — renders deterministically, no network, no rate limits.
#
# Requires a headless-capable chromium on PATH. The board pins "now" to the
# fixture's tick time in fixture mode, so re-runs produce identical frames.
#
# Usage: bash site/factory/visual-check/capture.sh
set -eu
cd "$(dirname "$0")/.."   # site/factory — the board root (fixture URLs are relative to it)

CHROME="${CHROME:-$(command -v chromium || command -v chromium-browser || command -v google-chrome)}"
BASE="file://$PWD/index.html"
OUT="visual-check"
FIXTURE="visual-check/fixture.json"

shot() { # shot <name> <w> <h> <query>
  local name="$1" w="$2" h="$3" q="$4"
  "$CHROME" --headless=new --no-sandbox --disable-gpu \
    --allow-file-access-from-files --hide-scrollbars \
    --window-size="$w,$h" --virtual-time-budget=5000 \
    --screenshot="$OUT/$name" "$BASE?$q" 2>/dev/null
  echo "  $name"
}

echo "capturing factory-board visual-check fixtures (fixture=$FIXTURE)"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.png"          1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.light.png"         1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=light"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.2048x1320.dark.png"         2048 1320 "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
shot "factory-board.visual-check.390x844.dark.mobile.png"    390  844  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark"
# the drawer is an overlay — captured open (deep-linked) as its own frame
shot "factory-board.visual-check.1440x900.dark.drawer.png"   1440 900  "fixture=$FIXTURE&theme=dark&drawer=pr-817@validating"
echo "done"

blocks.text:
# Factory Board v3 (site/factory)

Real-time-ish board for the SM machine: three factories side by side (tabs),
cards flowing through the full label pipeline — development → PR → review →
approved queue → validating → merged — with lifecycle timestamps, a mini
SVG timeline per card, readable per-lane progress, a details drawer
(state history + timings + token spend), and the issue backlog lanes.
Zero build, zero tokens, zero rate limits: the data is a JSON snapshot
each factory's SM tick publishes to its repo's `factory-data` branch
(raw.githubusercontent CDN link).

## Data flow

```
SM tick (sm_github.json, per factory repo)
  └─ end of pass: buildFactoryState() + publishFactoryState()
       └─ gh api PUT repos/O/R/contents/data/<asset>   (factory-data branch)
            └─ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/O/R/factory-data/data/<asset>
                 └─ board fetch() every refreshMs (schema 1 + 2 both render)
```

Factories on the board today:

| tab | repo | asset | state-publish |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| flutter_agent_harness | IstiN/flutter_agent_harness | `fa-state.json` | on |
| dmtools-dart | epam/dmtools-dart | `dart-state.json` | on |
| dmtools-agents | IstiN/dmtools-agents | `agents-state.json` | on |

## Deploy (any static host)

1. Copy this folder.
2. Edit `config.js` — factories[] (stateUrl, accent), lanes,
   backlogColumns, badgeLabels.
3. Style: only `:root` variables in `styles.css` (+ `data-theme="light"`
   overrides). Design tokens mirror `site/index.html` (slate palette,
   JetBrains Mono — embedded, no CDN). Embeddable via `?theme=light|dark`.

## Enable publishing for a factory (OPT-IN)

The machine workflow passes `state-publish` (JSON string) to factory-sm.yml:

```yaml
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
```

- `channel: 'release'` — the only channel today; anything else = off.
- `repo` — target repo (default: the tick's repo).
- `tag` — the data branch name (default `factory-data`; all three factories
  use it — the board URLs share the shape).
- `asset` — one asset per factory (`fa-state.json`, `dart-state.json`,
  `agents-state.json`).

## State schema (v2)

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "factory": "flutter_agent_harness",
  "repo": "IstiN/flutter_agent_harness",
  "tick": { "at": "...", "dryRun": false, "processed": ["pr-817"] },
  "checks": ["Quality gate", "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)", "Binaries smoke gate"],
  "lanes": {
    "development":   [ { "issue": 315, "title": "...", "labels": ["agent:dev"],
                         "url": "https://github.com/O/R/issues/315",
                         "devStartedAt": "..." } ],
    "pr_created":    [ { "pr": 870, "title": "...", "labels": [],
                         "prCreated": "...", "checks": null } ],
    "review":        [ { "pr": 860, "labels": ["ai_pr_reviewed"],
                         "prCreated": "...", "reviewedAt": "..." } ],
    "approved_queue":[ { "pr": 828, "queuePos": 1, "approvedAt": "..." } ],
    "validating":    [ { "pr": 817, "checks": { "verdict": "in_progress",
                         "at": "...", "url": "..." }, "validatingAt": "..." } ],
    "merged_recent": [ { "pr": 801, "mergedAt": "...", "approvedAt": "...",
                         "validatingAt": "..." } ]
  },
  "counts": { "development": 1, "pr_created": 1, "review": 1,
              "approved_queue": 1, "validating": 1, "merged_recent": 1 }
}
```

Lanes are a deterministic read of the machine labels (the same predicates
the reconcile rules query), in PIPELINE order: `agent:dev` (no
`ai_developed`) → development; open, no machine labels → pr_created;
`ai_pr_reviewed` → review; `pr_approved` → approved_queue (FIFO by PR
number, `queuePos` 1-based); `ai_validating` → validating (mutex); merged
within 24h → merged_recent.

Timestamps on every card (the v2 feature — the pipeline becomes measurable):

- `prCreated` / `mergedAt` — GitHub fields (`created_at` / `merged_at`),
  exact from the first snapshot.
- `reviewedAt` / `approvedAt` / `validatingAt` / `devStartedAt` — label
  transition times, accumulated tick-over-tick: the tick fetches the
  previous snapshot off the `factory-data` branch (one `gh api` call),
  carries forward what it stamped before, and stamps `now` on transitions
  it witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). Exact
  to the tick cadence (~10 min). First snapshot after the upgrade: these
  stay `null` until each card's next transition — honest unknowns, and the
  per-tick `<base>-history.json` snapshots keep the raw evidence.

The board renders schema 1 snapshots too (`fresh` maps onto `pr_created`,
timestamp chips simply don't render) — old history files never break it.

## v3 additions (owner 2026-10-03 — additive, schema stays 2)

Old snapshots render untouched; every new key is optional.

### `card.history` — state timeline (details drawer + timings)

Every card may carry `history: [{state, at}]` (oldest first), accumulated
tick-over-tick by the same mechanism as the v2 timestamps: carried
forward, appended when the tick witnesses a transition, capped at 24
entries. PR states are lane ids; issue states are backlog bucket ids.
The first entry after the upgrade carries no `at` (honest unknown). The
board falls back to deriving a timeline from the v2 timestamp fields when
`history` is absent, so pre-v3 snapshots still get a usable drawer.

### `backlog` — issues as board lanes

```json
"backlog": {
  "in_dev":  [ { "issue": 402, "title": "...", "assignee": "ai-teammate",
                 "labels": ["agent:dev"], "url": "...", "bucket": "in_dev",
                 "history": [...], "devStartedAt": "..." } ],
  "queued":  [], "blocked": [], "inbox": []
},
"backlogCounts": { "in_dev": 1, "queued": 0, "blocked": 0, "inbox": 0 }
```

Fed by ONE search call per tick (`repo:X is:issue is:open`). Bucketing is
a deterministic read of the machine's own signals, first match wins:

| bucket | signal |
| --- | --- |
| `blocked` | the `blocked` label — owner hold, its own visually distinct column |
| `in_dev` | assigned to the machine author (the `machineAuthor` deployment knob — a comma-separated login list, gh-728; unconfigured → no assignment bucketing at all) |
| `queued` | `agent:dev` label, not assigned |
| `inbox` | everything else (no label/assignee) |

**Page limit**: the search tool returns a single page (no `perPage` knob),
so a repo with more open issues than one page truncates at the source. Each
bucket is additionally capped at `BACKLOG_CAP` (50, newest kept) in
`js/factoryState.js` — the published snapshot stays bounded, and
`backlogCounts` always equal what the snapshot actually holds (a truncated
lane never masquerades as an empty one). A deployment with more issues than
that should narrow the query instead.

Issues carrying `ai_developed` have handed off to the PR side — they leave
the backlog (unless blocked). Backlog issues share one history array with
their development-lane twin, so the drawer tells the same story from both.

### `card.tokens` — OPTIONAL per-leg token spend

```json
"tokens": [ { "leg": "story_development", "at": "...", "prompt": 48210,
              "completion": 12980, "total": 61190 } ]
```

Keyed `pr-N` / `issue-N` in the builder's `tokens` input. Factories whose
legs report usage (fa's bench) drop a keyed JSON file into the tick's
checkout — `statePublish.tokensFile`, default
`outputs/token_usage/factory_tokens.json`; `readTokensFile()` picks it up
(or returns null on ANY miss — the tick never fails over tokens).
Factories that don't report tokens yet publish token-less cards and the
drawer renders `tokens — not reported by this factory`. The schema never
requires the key.

### Board surfaces

- **Lane summaries** — `N total · M done · K in-flight · Q queued` (+
  blocked) per lane, with a thin segmented progress bar (done / in-flight /
  queued / blocked). Done = merged; in-flight = dev leg running or mutex
  validating; queued = waiting on the next machine step; blocked = owner
  hold. Cards and timeline dots stay as decoration.
- **Details drawer** — click any PR/issue card: header (number, title,
  head sha, current state, labels, `open o…

Let me look at test_packVersionGuard.js briefly and also check `dmtools compile` pack behavior — the data file will ride the pack if packs include data files... Actually, pack publishing likely includes specific files. Let me check what a pack includes (setup/releasePacks?).

/**
 * Unit tests: the pack-release version guard (gh-812).
 *

 * changed underneath; 091304 republished a DIFFERENT sm_github-0.1.36.zip

 * caches ran mixed content — every fa machine-sm tick red for ~25 min.
 *
 * The guard (ci/pack_version_guard.cjs) encodes the gh-812 contract:
 *   V1 the shipped version beats the ledger — the release history is
 *      append-only and cannot lie; versions.json can (and did).

 *      version that is already out there with other content.
 *   V3 a rebuilt-but-unbumped agent whose payload differs from what its

blocks.text:
Interesting failures:

1. `__proto__ as a model id` — `parseModelPricing({ '__proto__': {input:1, output:2} })` returned null. Why? In the test I wrote the literal `{ '__proto__': {...} }` — in JavaScript, `{'__proto__': x}` in an object LITERAL sets the prototype, NOT a data property! So `Object.keys(parsed)` doesn't include '__proto__' — the parsed object has prototype {input, output} and no own keys. So `n=0`, defaultRates null → returns null. Hmm — so my test expectation is wrong for the LITERAL case: `{'__proto__': {...}}` as a literal is a prototype assignment. To create a real own '__proto__' data key you'd need `Object.defineProperty` or JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {...}}') — JSON.parse DOES create own property '__proto__'. So the untrusted-input path is JSON.parse — exactly the realistic path. Fix the TEST to use JSON.parse (realistic), which creates the own key.

But ALSO — my implementation must handle it: with JSON.parse, `Object.keys(parsed)` includes '__proto__' (own property). `rates[k] = e` on Object.create(null) — assignment of '__proto__' key on a prototype-less object creates an own data property. Good. But wait — does GraalJS handle `obj['__proto__'] = value` on a null-prototype object as a data property? Yes — no Object.prototype.__proto__ setter inherited. Good.

Let me fix the test to use JSON.parse.

2. `unknown model → model kept, cost omitted` — "nothing priced → no Σ$ rollup at all" failed: `st.costs` exists?! Why? priceTokens returns summary whenever `pricing` is set — even when NOTHING was priced (usd14d=0, pricedLegs=0). My test expects: unknown model → no costs key at all. Hmm. Which behavior do I want?

Think: pricing loaded + active, but this tick's ledger has no priced rows → header shows "Σ$0.00 · 14d"? Or nothing? My test said `assert.notOk('costs' in st, 'nothing priced → no Σ$ rollup at all')`. But wait — the global Σ$ is over the WHOLE ledger with a 14d window... if no rows priced, Σ$ genuinely is 0 for priced models. Hmm, but publishing `costs: {usd14d: 0, pricedLegs: 0}` means the header pill renders "Σ$0.00 · 14d" — which says "pricing live, zero priced spend". vs absent = "pricing off". 

Which is better? For the board: hiding when nothing priced avoids a confusing "$0.00" on factories where the pricing table exists but models don't match (e.g. pre-fa#1460 — models all empty → nothing priced → don't show $0.00). That's actually important: pre-fa#1460, ALL rows have model:null → pricedLegs 0 → showing "Σ$0.00" would be misleading ("everything free?"). So: publish `costs` only when pricedLegs > 0. That's what my test demands and it's the right call. Implementation: in buildFactoryState, `if (costs && costs.pricedLegs > 0) state.costs = costs;` — or in priceTokens return null when pricedLegs===0? No — keep priceTokens returning the summary (pure), gate at the snapshot attach. Hmm — but the "Σ$ rounds to cents" test expects usd14d=0.18 > 0 fine. And "undated rows" test: `st.costs.usd14d` = 0 with pricedLegs 0 — WAIT that test does `assert.equal(st.costs.usd14d, 0)` — it EXPECTS st.costs to exist with usd14d 0! Conflict!

Let me re-read my undated test:
```js
test('undated rows still price per-row but stay out of the Σ$ window (honest unknown)', ...
    assert.equal(cardFor(st, 31).tokens[0].cost, 3);
    assert.equal(st.costs.usd14d, 0);
    assert.equal(st.costs.pricedLegs, 0);
```
Here pricedLegs=0 (undated → out of window) but I expect st.costs to EXIST with usd14d=0. Hmm — inconsistent with the "unknown model → no costs" test? In the undated case the model IS known and priced — the ledger HAS priced spend, it's just not placeable in the window. So showing "Σ$0.00 · 14d · 0 priced legs" would... hmm. Actually what should the header show there? The rows are priced ($3 per row visible on cards) but the 14d rollup can't count them (no dates) → header Σ$ = 0.00. Is showing "Σ$0.00" while a card shows "$3.00" contradictory? A tooltip could explain... This is getting too subtle. Let me simplify to a coherent rule:

**Rule: the snapshot carries `costs` iff pricing is loaded AND at least one row priced (cost attached).** usd14d = Σ in-window; pricedLegs = rows priced in-window.

- unknown model only → no rows priced → no costs. ✔ (test 2)
- absent model only → no costs. ✔ (test 3)
- undated rows priced → rows priced (>0) → costs EXISTS, usd14d=0, pricedLegs=0. ✔ (test 4 — header shows $0.00; per-row $ shows on cards; acceptable, honest: the rollup window can't place them)

Hmm wait, but is that inconsistent-looking? pricedLegs means "in-window priced legs" — undated priced rows aren't counted. The header tooltip says "N priced legs (14d)". It's coherent: the costs block is the 14d-window rollup; its zeros mean "nothing in the window". The GATE for showing the block is "pricing produced at least one $ anywhere" — i.e., pricing is live and matching. OK.

So implementation: `if (costs && (costs.pricedLegs > 0 || ...))` — hmm, undated case: pricedLegs=0 but a row HAS cost. Gate should be "any row priced". Let me track that separately: `summary.priced = true` when any row gets cost? Or count total priced rows regardless of window: add `pricedRows` (all) vs `pricedLegs` (in-window)? Simpler: gate on "any cost attached" via a private flag. Hmm — but flag in summary leaks to snapshot. Use a local var in priceTokens:

```js
var any = false;
... row.cost = cost; any = true;
...
if (!any) return null;
return summary;
```
Wait — but then priceTokens returns null when no rows priced — and buildFactoryState `if (costs) state.costs = costs` suffices. And the undated test: any=true → costs exists, usd14d 0, pricedLegs 0 ✔. Unknown-model test: any=false → null → no costs ✔. Clean. And priceTokens pure semantics: null = "nothing priced".

3. `multi-key ledger` test failure — let me see the actual message. It failed at line `assert.notOk('cost' in cardFor(st, 31).tokens[1], 'stale row keeps model, drops cost? NO...')` — my own test comment is confusing; I wrote the assertion then contradicted it in the message and then asserted cost===3. That first notOk is WRONG (per-row cost stays regardless of window — that's my design). Remove that stray assertion (it was leftover thinking). The next line asserts equality 3 — correct behavior. Fix the test.

Wait, let me recheck what the failure message was — "expected falsy, got: true" for absent-model test = 'cost' in row is true?? For the ABSENT model test: `assert.notOk('cost' in cardFor(st, 31).tokens[0])` got true — cost attached to a model-less row?! Why? ratesFor(pricing, null)... let me re-check ratesFor:

```js
function ratesFor(pricing, model) {
    if (!pricing || model == null || model === '') return null;
```
model null → return null. priceTokens: `if (!row || row.model == null) return;` — skips before ratesFor. So cost shouldn't attach... unless the failure is from a DIFFERENT assertion in that test. The message "expected falsy, got: true" — could be `assert.notOk('costs' in st)` → 'costs' in st is true — because priceTokens returns a summary whenever pricing is set (the bug identified above, failure mode #2). Yes! Same root cause. OK.

So fixes:
- Test: `__proto__` test → build via JSON.parse.
- Test: multi-key → drop the stray notOk line.
- Impl: priceTokens returns null when no row was priced (gate via `any`).

Let me apply.

Root causes identified: (1) the `__proto__` test must use JSON.parse (an object literal `{'__proto__':...}` sets a prototype, not an own key — JSON.parse is the realistic untrusted path), (2) `priceTokens` must return null when nothing priced (no misleading "$0.00" header pre-fa#1460), (3) a stray contradictory assertion in my multi-key test. Fixing:

blocks.text:
# Factory Board v3 (site/factory)

Real-time-ish board for the SM machine: three factories side by side (tabs),
cards flowing through the full label pipeline — development → PR → review →
approved queue → validating → merged — with lifecycle timestamps, a mini
SVG timeline per card, readable per-lane progress, a details drawer
(state history + timings + token spend), and the issue backlog lanes.
Zero build, zero tokens, zero rate limits: the data is a JSON snapshot
each factory's SM tick publishes to its repo's `factory-data` branch
(raw.githubusercontent CDN link).

## Data flow

```
SM tick (sm_github.json, per factory repo)
  └─ end of pass: buildFactoryState() + publishFactoryState()
       └─ gh api PUT repos/O/R/contents/data/<asset>   (factory-data branch)
            └─ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/O/R/factory-data/data/<asset>
                 └─ board fetch() every refreshMs (schema 1 + 2 both render)
```

Factories on the board today:

| tab | repo | asset | state-publish |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| flutter_agent_harness | IstiN/flutter_agent_harness | `fa-state.json` | on |
| dmtools-dart | epam/dmtools-dart | `dart-state.json` | on |
| dmtools-agents | IstiN/dmtools-agents | `agents-state.json` | on |

## Deploy (any static host)

1. Copy this folder.
2. Edit `config.js` — factories[] (stateUrl, accent), lanes,
   backlogColumns, badgeLabels.
3. Style: only `:root` variables in `styles.css` (+ `data-theme="light"`
   overrides). Design tokens mirror `site/index.html` (slate palette,
   JetBrains Mono — embedded, no CDN). Embeddable via `?theme=light|dark`.

## Enable publishing for a factory (OPT-IN)

The machine workflow passes `state-publish` (JSON string) to factory-sm.yml:

```yaml
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
```

- `channel: 'release'` — the only channel today; anything else = off.
- `repo` — target repo (default: the tick's repo).
- `tag` — the data branch name (default `factory-data`; all three factories
  use it — the board URLs share the shape).
- `asset` — one asset per factory (`fa-state.json`, `dart-state.json`,
  `agents-state.json`).

## State schema (v2)

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "factory": "flutter_agent_harness",
  "repo": "IstiN/flutter_agent_harness",
  "tick": { "at": "...", "dryRun": false, "processed": ["pr-817"] },
  "checks": ["Quality gate", "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)", "Binaries smoke gate"],
  "lanes": {
    "development":   [ { "issue": 315, "title": "...", "labels": ["agent:dev"],
                         "url": "https://github.com/O/R/issues/315",
                         "devStartedAt": "..." } ],
    "pr_created":    [ { "pr": 870, "title": "...", "labels": [],
                         "prCreated": "...", "checks": null } ],
    "review":        [ { "pr": 860, "labels": ["ai_pr_reviewed"],
                         "prCreated": "...", "reviewedAt": "..." } ],
    "approved_queue":[ { "pr": 828, "queuePos": 1, "approvedAt": "..." } ],
    "validating":    [ { "pr": 817, "checks": { "verdict": "in_progress",
                         "at": "...", "url": "..." }, "validatingAt": "..." } ],
    "merged_recent": [ { "pr": 801, "mergedAt": "...", "approvedAt": "...",
                         "validatingAt": "..." } ]
  },
  "counts": { "development": 1, "pr_created": 1, "review": 1,
              "approved_queue": 1, "validating": 1, "merged_recent": 1 }
}
```

Lanes are a deterministic read of the machine labels (the same predicates
the reconcile rules query), in PIPELINE order: `agent:dev` (no
`ai_developed`) → development; open, no machine labels → pr_created;
`ai_pr_reviewed` → review; `pr_approved` → approved_queue (FIFO by PR
number, `queuePos` 1-based); `ai_validating` → validating (mutex); merged
within 24h → merged_recent.

Timestamps on every card (the v2 feature — the pipeline becomes measurable):

- `prCreated` / `mergedAt` — GitHub fields (`created_at` / `merged_at`),
  exact from the first snapshot.
- `reviewedAt` / `approvedAt` / `validatingAt` / `devStartedAt` — label
  transition times, accumulated tick-over-tick: the tick fetches the
  previous snapshot off the `factory-data` branch (one `gh api` call),
  carries forward what it stamped before, and stamps `now` on transitions
  it witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). Exact
  to the tick cadence (~10 min). First snapshot after the upgrade: these
  stay `null` until each card's next transition — honest unknowns, and the
  per-tick `<base>-history.json` snapshots keep the raw evidence.

The board renders schema 1 snapshots too (`fresh` maps onto `pr_created`,
timestamp chips simply don't render) — old history files never break it.

## v3 additions (owner 2026-10-03 — additive, schema stays 2)

Old snapshots render untouched; every new key is optional.

### `card.history` — state timeline (details drawer + timings)

Every card may carry `history: [{state, at}]` (oldest first), accumulated
tick-over-tick by the same mechanism as the v2 timestamps: carried
forward, appended when the tick witnesses a transition, capped at 24
entries. PR states are lane ids; issue states are backlog bucket ids.
The first entry after the upgrade carries no `at` (honest unknown). The
board falls back to deriving a timeline from the v2 timestamp fields when
`history` is absent, so pre-v3 snapshots still get a usable drawer.

### `backlog` — issues as board lanes

```json
"backlog": {
  "in_dev":  [ { "issue": 402, "title": "...", "assignee": "ai-teammate",
                 "labels": ["agent:dev"], "url": "...", "bucket": "in_dev",
                 "history": [...], "devStartedAt": "..." } ],
  "queued":  [], "blocked": [], "inbox": []
},
"backlogCounts": { "in_dev": 1, "queued": 0, "blocked": 0, "inbox": 0 }
```

Fed by ONE search call per tick (`repo:X is:issue is:open`). Bucketing is
a deterministic read of the machine's own signals, first match wins:

| bucket | signal |
| --- | --- |
| `blocked` | the `blocked` label — owner hold, its own visually distinct column |
| `in_dev` | assigned to the machine author (the `machineAuthor` deployment knob — a comma-separated login list, gh-728; unconfigured → no assignment bucketing at all) |
| `queued` | `agent:dev` label, not assigned |
| `inbox` | everything else (no label/assignee) |

**Page limit**: the search tool returns a single page (no `perPage` knob),
so a repo with more open issues than one page truncates at the source. Each
bucket is additionally capped at `BACKLOG_CAP` (50, newest kept) in
`js/factoryState.js` — the published snapshot stays bounded, and
`backlogCounts` always equal what the snapshot actually holds (a truncated
lane never masquerades as an empty one). A deployment with more issues than
that should narrow the query instead.

Issues carrying `ai_developed` have handed off to the PR side — they leave
the backlog (unless blocked). Backlog issues share one history array with
their development-lane twin, so the drawer tells the same story from both.

### `card.tokens` — OPTIONAL per-leg token spend

```json
"tokens": [ { "leg": "story_development", "at": "...", "prompt": 48210,

```

blocks.text:
Interesting failures:

1. `__proto__ as a model id` — `parseModelPricing({ '__proto__': {input:1, output:2} })` returned null. Why? In the test I wrote the literal `{ '__proto__': {...} }` — in JavaScript, `{'__proto__': x}` in an object LITERAL sets the prototype, NOT a data property! So `Object.keys(parsed)` doesn't include '__proto__' — the parsed object has prototype {input, output} and no own keys. So `n=0`, defaultRates null → returns null. Hmm — so my test expectation is wrong for the LITERAL case: `{'__proto__': {...}}` as a literal is a prototype assignment. To create a real own '__proto__' data key you'd need `Object.defineProperty` or JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {...}}') — JSON.parse DOES create own property '__proto__'. So the untrusted-input path is JSON.parse — exactly the realistic path. Fix the TEST to use JSON.parse (realistic), which creates the own key.

But ALSO — my implementation must handle it: with JSON.parse, `Object.keys(parsed)` includes '__proto__' (own property). `rates[k] = e` on Object.create(null) — assignment of '__proto__' key on a prototype-less object creates an own data property. Good. But wait — does GraalJS handle `obj['__proto__'] = value` on a null-prototype object as a data property? Yes — no Object.prototype.__proto__ setter inherited. Good.

Let me fix the test to use JSON.parse.

2. `unknown model → model kept, cost omitted` — "nothing priced → no Σ$ rollup at all" failed: `st.costs` exists?! Why? priceTokens returns summary whenever `pricing` is set — even when NOTHING was priced (usd14d=0, pricedLegs=0). My test expects: unknown model → no costs key at all. Hmm. Which behavior do I want?

Think: pricing loaded + active, but this tick's ledger has no priced rows → header shows "Σ$0.00 · 14d"? Or nothing? My test said `assert.notOk('costs' in st, 'nothing priced → no Σ$ rollup at all')`. But wait — the global Σ$ is over the WHOLE ledger with a 14d window... if no rows priced, Σ$ genuinely is 0 for priced models. Hmm, but publishing `costs: {usd14d: 0, pricedLegs: 0}` means the header pill renders "Σ$0.00 · 14d" — which says "pricing live, zero priced spend". vs absent = "pricing off". 

Which is better? For the board: hiding when nothing priced avoids a confusing "$0.00" on factories where the pricing table exists but models don't match (e.g. pre-fa#1460 — models all empty → nothing priced → don't show $0.00). That's actually important: pre-fa#1460, ALL rows have model:null → pricedLegs 0 → showing "Σ$0.00" would be misleading ("everything free?"). So: publish `costs` only when pricedLegs > 0. That's what my test demands and it's the right call. Implementation: in buildFactoryState, `if (costs && costs.pricedLegs > 0) state.costs = costs;` — or in priceTokens return null when pricedLegs===0? No — keep priceTokens returning the summary (pure), gate at the snapshot attach. Hmm — but the "Σ$ rounds to cents" test expects usd14d=0.18 > 0 fine. And "undated rows" test: `st.costs.usd14d` = 0 with pricedLegs 0 — WAIT that test does `assert.equal(st.costs.usd14d, 0)` — it EXPECTS st.costs to exist with usd14d 0! Conflict!

Let me re-read my undated test:
```js
test('undated rows still price per-row but stay out of the Σ$ window (honest unknown)', ...
    assert.equal(cardFor(st, 31).tokens[0].cost, 3);
    assert.equal(st.costs.usd14d, 0);
    assert.equal(st.costs.pricedLegs, 0);
```
Here pricedLegs=0 (undated → out of window) but I expect st.costs to EXIST with usd14d=0. Hmm — inconsistent with the "unknown model → no costs" test? In the undated case the model IS known and priced — the ledger HAS priced spend, it's just not placeable in the window. So showing "Σ$0.00 · 14d · 0 priced legs" would... hmm. Actually what should the header show there? The rows are priced ($3 per row visible on cards) but the 14d rollup can't count them (no dates) → header Σ$ = 0.00. Is showing "Σ$0.00" while a card shows "$3.00" contradictory? A tooltip could explain... This is getting too subtle. Let me simplify to a coherent rule:

**Rule: the snapshot carries `costs` iff pricing is loaded AND at least one row priced (cost attached).** usd14d = Σ in-window; pricedLegs = rows priced in-window.

- unknown model only → no rows priced → no costs. ✔ (test 2)
- absent model only → no costs. ✔ (test 3)
- undated rows priced → rows priced (>0) → costs EXISTS, usd14d=0, pricedLegs=0. ✔ (test 4 — header shows $0.00; per-row $ shows on cards; acceptable, honest: the rollup window can't place them)

Hmm wait, but is that inconsistent-looking? pricedLegs means "in-window priced legs" — undated priced rows aren't counted. The header tooltip says "N priced legs (14d)". It's coherent: the costs block is the 14d-window rollup; its zeros mean "nothing in the window". The GATE for showing the block is "pricing produced at least one $ anywhere" — i.e., pricing is live and matching. OK.

So implementation: `if (costs && (costs.pricedLegs > 0 || ...))` — hmm, undated case: pricedLegs=0 but a row HAS cost. Gate should be "any row priced". Let me track that separately: `summary.priced = true` when any row gets cost? Or count total priced rows regardless of window: add `pricedRows` (all) vs `pricedLegs` (in-window)? Simpler: gate on "any cost attached" via a private flag. Hmm — but flag in summary leaks to snapshot. Use a local var in priceTokens:

```js
var any = false;
... row.cost = cost; any = true;
...
if (!any) return null;
return summary;
```
Wait — but then priceTokens returns null when no rows priced — and buildFactoryState `if (costs) state.costs = costs` suffices. And the undated test: any=true → costs exists, usd14d 0, pricedLegs 0 ✔. Unknown-model test: any=false → null → no costs ✔. Clean. And priceTokens pure semantics: null = "nothing priced".

3. `multi-key ledger` test failure — let me see the actual message. It failed at line `assert.notOk('cost' in cardFor(st, 31).tokens[1], 'stale row keeps model, drops cost? NO...')` — my own test comment is confusing; I wrote the assertion then contradicted it in the message and then asserted cost===3. That first notOk is WRONG (per-row cost stays regardless of window — that's my design). Remove that stray assertion (it was leftover thinking). The next line asserts equality 3 — correct behavior. Fix the test.

Wait, let me recheck what the failure message was — "expected falsy, got: true" for absent-model test = 'cost' in row is true?? For the ABSENT model test: `assert.notOk('cost' in cardFor(st, 31).tokens[0])` got true — cost attached to a model-less row?! Why? ratesFor(pricing, null)... let me re-check ratesFor:

```js
function ratesFor(pricing, model) {
    if (!pricing || model == null || model === '') return null;
```
model null → return null. priceTokens: `if (!row || row.model == null) return;` — skips before ratesFor. So cost shouldn't attach... unless the failure is from a DIFFERENT assertion in that test. The message "expected falsy, got: true" — could be `assert.notOk('costs' in st)` → 'costs' in st is true — because priceTokens returns a summary whenever pricing is set (the bug identified above, failure mode #2). Yes! Same root cause. OK.

So fixes:
- Test: `__proto__` test → build via JSON.parse.
- Test: multi-key → drop the stray notOk line.
- Impl: priceTokens returns null when no row was priced (gate via `any`).

Let me apply.

Root causes identified: (1) the `__proto__` test must use JSON.parse (an object literal `{'__proto__':...}` sets a prototype, not an own key — JSON.parse is the realistic untrusted path), (2) `priceTokens` must return null when nothing priced (no misleading "$0.00" header pre-fa#1460), (3) a stray contradictory assertion in my multi-key test. Fixing:

blocks.text:
# Factory Board v3 (site/factory)

Real-time-ish board for the SM machine: three factories side by side (tabs),
cards flowing through the full label pipeline — development → PR → review →
approved queue → validating → merged — with lifecycle timestamps, a mini
SVG timeline per card, readable per-lane progress, a details drawer
(state history + timings + token spend), and the issue backlog lanes.
Zero build, zero tokens, zero rate limits: the data is a JSON snapshot
each factory's SM tick publishes to its repo's `factory-data` branch
(raw.githubusercontent CDN link).

## Data flow

```
SM tick (sm_github.json, per factory repo)
  └─ end of pass: buildFactoryState() + publishFactoryState()
       └─ gh api PUT repos/O/R/contents/data/<asset>   (factory-data branch)
            └─ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/O/R/factory-data/data/<asset>
                 └─ board fetch() every refreshMs (schema 1 + 2 both render)
```

Factories on the board today:

| tab | repo | asset | state-publish |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| flutter_agent_harness | IstiN/flutter_agent_harness | `fa-state.json` | on |
| dmtools-dart | epam/dmtools-dart | `dart-state.json` | on |
| dmtools-agents | IstiN/dmtools-agents | `agents-state.json` | on |

## Deploy (any static host)

1. Copy this folder.
2. Edit `config.js` — factories[] (stateUrl, accent), lanes,
   backlogColumns, badgeLabels.
3. Style: only `:root` variables in `styles.css` (+ `data-theme="light"`
   overrides). Design tokens mirror `site/index.html` (slate palette,
   JetBrains Mono — embedded, no CDN). Embeddable via `?theme=light|dark`.

## Enable publishing for a factory (OPT-IN)

The machine workflow passes `state-publish` (JSON string) to factory-sm.yml:

```yaml
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
```

- `channel: 'release'` — the only channel today; anything else = off.

```json
{
  "schema": 2,
  "factory": "flutter_agent_harness",
  "repo": "IstiN/flutter_agent_harness",
  "tick": { "at": "...", "dryRun": false, "processed": ["pr-817"] },
  "checks": ["Quality gate", "JS engine integration (quickjs-ng)", "Binaries smoke gate"],
  "lanes": {
    "development":   [ { "issue": 315, "title": "...", "labels": ["agent:dev"],

                         "devStartedAt": "..." } ],
    "pr_created":    [ { "pr": 870, "title": "...", "labels": [],
                         "prCreated": "...", "checks": null } ],
    "review":        [ { "pr": 860, "labels": ["ai_pr_reviewed"],
                         "prCreated": "...", "reviewedAt": "..." } ],
    "approved_queue":[ { "pr": 828, "queuePos": 1, "approvedAt": "..." } ],
    "validating":    [ { "pr": 817, "checks": { "verdict": "in_progress",
                         "at": "...", "url": "..." }, "validatingAt": "..." } ],
    "merged_recent": [ { "pr": 801, "mergedAt": "...", "approvedAt": "...",
                         "validatingAt": "..." } ]
  },
  "counts": { "development": 1, "pr_created": 1, "review": 1,
              "approved_queue": 1, "validating": 1, "merged_recent": 1 }
}
```

Lanes are a deterministic read of the machine labels (the same predicates
the reconcile rules query), in PIPELINE order: `agent:dev` (no
`ai_developed`) → development; open, no machine labels → pr_created;
`ai_pr_reviewed` → review; `pr_approved` → approved_queue (FIFO by PR
number, `queuePos` 1-based); `ai_validating` → validating (mutex); merged
within 24h → merged_recent.

Timestamps on every card (the v2 feature — the pipeline becomes measurable):

- `prCreated` / `mergedAt` — GitHub fields (`created_at` / `merged_at`),
  exact from the first snapshot.
- `reviewedAt` / `approvedAt` / `validatingAt` / `devStartedAt` — label
  transition times, accumulated tick-over-tick: the tick fetches the
  previous snapshot off the `factory-data` branch (one `gh api` call),
  carries forward what it stamped before, and stamps `now` on transitions
  it witnesses (label present now, absent in the previous snapshot). Exact
  to the tick cadence (~10 min). First snapshot after the upgrade: these
  stay `null` until each card's next transition — honest unknowns, and the
  per-tick `<base>-history.json` snapshots keep the raw evidence.

The board renders schema 1 snapshots too (`fresh` maps onto `pr_created`,
timestamp chips simply don't render) — old history files never break it.

## v3 additions (owner 2026-10-03 — additive, schema stays 2)

Old snapshots render untouched; every new key is optional.

### `card.history` — state timeline (details drawer + timings)

Every card may carry `history: [{state, at}]` (oldest first), accumulated
tick-over-tick by the same mechanism as the v2 timestamps: carried
forward, appended when the tick witnesses a transition, capped at 24
entries. PR states are lane ids; issue states are backlog bucket ids.
The first entry after the upgrade carries no `at` (honest unknown). The
board falls back to deriving a timeline from the v2 timestamp fields when
`history` is absent, so pre-v3 snapshots still get a usable drawer.

### `backlog` — issues as board lanes

```json
"backlog": {
  "in_dev":  [ { "issue": 402, "title": "...", "assignee": "ai-teammate",
                 "labels": ["agent:dev"], "url": "...", "bucket": "in_dev",
                 "history": [...], "devStartedAt": "..." } ],
  "queued":  [], "blocked": [], "inbox": []
},
"backlogCounts": { "in_dev": 1, "queued": 0, "blocked": 0, "inbox": 0 }
```

Fed by ONE search call per tick (`repo:X is:issue is:open`). Bucketing is
a deterministic read of the machine's own signals, first match wins:

| bucket | signal |
| --- | --- |
| `blocked` | the `blocked` label — owner hold, its own visually distinct column |
| `in_dev` | assigned to the machine author (the `machineAuthor` deployment knob — a comma-separated login list, gh-728; unconfigured → no assignment bucketing at all) |
| `queued` | `agent:dev` label, not assigned |
| `inbox` | everything else (no label/assignee) |

**Page limit**: the search tool returns a single page (no `perPage` knob),
so a repo with more open issues than one page truncates at the source. Each
bucket is additionally capped at `BACKLOG_CAP` (50, newest kept) in
`js/factoryState.js` — the published snapshot stays bounded, and
`backlogCounts` always equal what the snapshot actually holds (a truncated
lane never masquerades as an empty one). A deployment with more issues than
that should narrow the query instead.

Issues carrying `ai_developed` have handed off to the PR side — they leave
the backlog (unless blocked). Backlog issues share one history array with
their development-lane twin, so the drawer tells the same story from both.

requires the key.

blocks.text:
# Factory Board v3 (site/factory)

Real-time-ish board for the SM machine: three factories side by side (tabs),
cards flowing through the full label pipeline — development → PR → review →
approved queue → validating → merged — with lifecycle timestamps, a mini
SVG timeline per card, readable per-lane progress, a details drawer
(state history + timings + token spend), and the issue backlog lanes.
Zero build, zero tokens, zero rate limits: the data is a JSON snapshot
each factory's SM tick publishes to its repo's `factory-data` branch
(raw.githubusercontent CDN link).

## Data flow

```
SM tick (sm_github.json, per factory repo)
  └─ end of pass: buildFactoryState() + publishFactoryState()
       └─ gh api PUT repos/O/R/contents/data/<asset>   (factory-data branch)
            └─ https://raw.githubusercontent.com/O/R/factory-data/data/<asset>
                 └─ board fetch() every refreshMs (schema 1 + 2 both render)
```

Factories on the board today:

| tab | repo | asset | state-publish |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| flutter_agent_harness | IstiN/flutter_agent_harness | `fa-state.json` | on |
| dmtools-dart | epam/dmtools-dart | `dart-state.json` | on |
| dmtools-agents | IstiN/dmtools-agents | `agents-state.json` | on |

## Deploy (any static host)

1. Copy this folder.
2. Edit `config.js` — factories[] (stateUrl, accent), lanes,
   backlogColumns, badgeLabels.
3. Style: only `:root` variables in `styles.css` (+ `data-theme="light"`
   overrides). Design tokens mirror `site/index.html` (slate palette,
   JetBrains Mono — embedded, no CDN). Embeddable via `?theme=light|dark`.

## Enable publishing for a factory (OPT-IN)

The machine workflow passes `state-publish` (JSON string) to factory-sm.yml:

```yaml
      state-publish: '{"channel":"release","tag":"factory-data","asset":"fa-state.json"}'
```

- `channel: 'release'` — the only channel today; anything else = off.
- `repo` — target repo (default: the tick's repo).
- `tag` — the data branch name (default `factory-data`; all three factories
  use it — the board URLs share the shape).
- `asset` — one asset per factory (`fa-state.json`, `dart-state.json`,
  `agents-state.json`).

## State schema (v2)

```json
{
  "schema": 2,

  "repo": "IstiN/flutter_agent_harness",

blocks.text:
Interesting failures:

1. `__proto__ as a model id` — `parseModelPricing({ '__proto__': {input:1, output:2} })` returned null. Why? In the test I wrote the literal `{ '__proto__': {...} }` — in JavaScript, `{'__proto__': x}` in an object LITERAL sets the prototype, NOT a data property! So `Object.keys(parsed)` doesn't include '__proto__' — the parsed object has prototype {input, output} and no own keys. So `n=0`, defaultRates null → returns null. Hmm — so my test expectation is wrong for the LITERAL case: `{'__proto__': {...}}` as a literal is a prototype assignment. To create a real own '__proto__' data key you'd need `Object.defineProperty` or JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {...}}') — JSON.parse DOES create own property '__proto__'. So the untrusted-input path is JSON.parse — exactly the realistic path. Fix the TEST to use JSON.parse (realistic), which creates the own key.

But ALSO — my implementation must handle it: with JSON.parse, `Object.keys(parsed)` includes '__proto__' (own property). `rates[k] = e` on Object.create(null) — assignment of '__proto__' key on a prototype-less object creates an own data property. Good. But wait — does GraalJS handle `obj['__proto__'] = value` on a null-prototype object as a data property? Yes — no Object.prototype.__proto__ setter inherited. Good.

Let me fix the test to use JSON.parse.

2. `unknown model → model kept, cost omitted` — "nothing priced → no Σ$ rollup at all" failed: `st.costs` exists?! Why? priceTokens returns summary whenever `pricing` is set — even when NOTHING was priced (usd14d=0, pricedLegs=0). My test expects: unknown model → no costs key at all. Hmm. Which behavior do I want?

Think: pricing loaded + active, but this tick's ledger has no priced rows → header shows "Σ$0.00 · 14d"? Or nothing? My test said `assert.notOk('costs' in st, 'nothing priced → no Σ$ rollup at all')`. But wait — the global Σ$ is over the WHOLE ledger with a 14d window... if no rows priced, Σ$ genuinely is 0 for priced models. Hmm, but publishing `costs: {usd14d: 0, pricedLegs: 0}` means the header pill renders "Σ$0.00 · 14d" — which says "pricing live, zero priced spend". vs absent = "pricing off". 

Which is better? For the board: hiding when nothing priced avoids a confusing "$0.00" on factories where the pricing table exists but models don't match (e.g. pre-fa#1460 — models all empty → nothing priced → don't show $0.00). That's actually important: pre-fa#1460, ALL rows have model:null → pricedLegs 0 → showing "Σ$0.00" would be misleading ("everything free?"). So: publish `costs` only when pricedLegs > 0. That's what my test demands and it's the right call. Implementation: in buildFactoryState, `if (costs && costs.pricedLegs > 0) state.costs = costs;` — or in priceTokens return null when pricedLegs===0? No — keep priceTokens returning the summary (pure), gate at the snapshot attach. Hmm — but the "Σ$ rounds to cents" test expects usd14d=0.18 > 0 fine. And "undated rows" test: `st.costs.usd14d` = 0 with pricedLegs 0 — WAIT that test does `assert.equal(st.costs.usd14d, 0)` — it EXPECTS st.costs to exist with usd14d 0! Conflict!

Let me re-read my undated test:
```js
test('undated rows still price per-row but stay out of the Σ$ window (honest unknown)', ...
    assert.equal(cardFor(st, 31).tokens[0].cost, 3);
    assert.equal(st.costs.usd14d, 0);
    assert.equal(st.costs.pricedLegs, 0);
```
Here pricedLegs=0 (undated → out of window) but I expect st.costs to EXIST with usd14d=0. Hmm — inconsistent with the "unknown model → no costs" test? In the undated case the model IS known and priced — the ledger HAS priced spend, it's just not placeable in the window. So showing "Σ$0.00 · 14d · 0 priced legs" would... hmm. Actually what should the header show there? The rows are priced ($3 per row visible on cards) but the 14d rollup can't count them (no dates) → header Σ$ = 0.00. Is showing "Σ$0.00" while a card shows "$3.00" contradictory? A tooltip could explain... This is getting too subtle. Let me simplify to a coherent rule:

**Rule: the snapshot carries `costs` iff pricing is loaded AND at least one row priced (cost attached).** usd14d = Σ in-window; pricedLegs = rows priced in-window.

- unknown model only → no rows priced → no costs. ✔ (test 2)
- absent model only → no costs. ✔ (test 3)
- undated rows priced → rows priced (>0) → costs EXISTS, usd14d=0, pricedLegs=0. ✔ (test 4 — header shows $0.00; per-row $ shows on cards; acceptable, honest: the rollup window can't place them)

Hmm wait, but is that inconsistent-looking? pricedLegs means "in-window priced legs" — undated priced rows aren't counted. The header tooltip says "N priced legs (14d)". It's coherent: the costs block is the 14d-window rollup; its zeros mean "nothing in the window". The GATE for showing the block is "pricing produced at least one $ anywhere" — i.e., pricing is live and matching. OK.

So implementation: `if (costs && (costs.pricedLegs > 0 || ...))` — hmm, undated case: pricedLegs=0 but a row HAS cost. Gate should be "any row priced". Let me track that separately: `summary.priced = true` when any row gets cost? Or count total priced rows regardless of window: add `pricedRows` (all) vs `pricedLegs` (in-window)? Simpler: gate on "any cost attached" via a private flag. Hmm — but flag in summary leaks to snapshot. Use a local var in priceTokens:

```js
var any = false;
... row.cost = cost; any = true;
...
if (!any) return null;
return summary;
```
Wait — but then priceTokens returns null when no rows priced — and buildFactoryState `if (costs) state.costs = costs` suffices. And the undated test: any=true → costs exists, usd14d 0, pricedLegs 0 ✔. Unknown-model test: any=false → null → no costs ✔. Clean. And priceTokens pure semantics: null = "nothing priced".

3. `multi-key ledger` test failure — let me see the actual message. It failed at line `assert.notOk('cost' in cardFor(st, 31).tokens[1], 'stale row keeps model, drops cost? NO...')` — my own test comment is confusing; I wrote the assertion then contradicted it in the message and then asserted cost===3. Fix the test.

For the ABSENT model test: `assert.notOk('cost' in cardFor(st, 31).tokens[0])` got true — cost attached to a model-less row?! Why? ratesFor(pricing, null)... let me re-check ratesFor:

```js
function ratesFor(pricing, model) {
    if (!pricing || model == null || model === '') return null;
```
model null → return null. priceTokens: `if (!row || row.model == null) return;` — skips before ratesFor. So cost shouldn't attach... unless the failure is from a DIFFERENT assertion in that test. The message "expected falsy, got: true" — could be `assert.notOk('costs' in st)` → 'costs' in st is true — because priceTokens returns a summary whenever pricing is set (the bug identified above, failure mode #2). Yes! Same root cause. OK.

blocks.text:
Interesting failures:

1. `__proto__ as a model id` — `parseModelPricing({ '__proto__': {input:1, output:2} })` returned null. Why? In the test I wrote the literal `{ '__proto__': {...} }` — in JavaScript, `{'__proto__': x}` in an object LITERAL sets the prototype, NOT a data property! So `Object.keys(parsed)` doesn't include '__proto__' — the parsed object has prototype {input, output} and no own keys. So `n=0`, defaultRates null → returns null. Hmm — so my test expectation is wrong for the LITERAL case: `{'__proto__': {...}}` as a literal is a prototype assignment. To create a real own '__proto__' data key you'd need `Object.defineProperty` or JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {...}}') — JSON.parse DOES create own property '__proto__'. So the untrusted-input path is JSON.parse — exactly the realistic path. Fix the TEST to use JSON.parse (realistic), which creates the own key.

But ALSO — my implementation must handle it: with JSON.parse, `Object.keys(parsed)` includes '__proto__' (own property). `rates[k] = e` on Object.create(null) — assignment of '__proto__' key on a prototype-less object creates an own data property. Good. But wait — does GraalJS handle `obj['__proto__'] = value` on a null-prototype object as a data property? Yes — no Object.prototype.__proto__ setter inherited. Good.

Let me fix the test to use JSON.parse.

2. `unknown model → model kept, cost omitted` — "nothing priced → no Σ$ rollup at all" failed: `st.costs` exists?! Why? priceTokens returns summary whenever `pricing` is set — even when NOTHING was priced (usd14d=0, pricedLegs=0). My test expects: unknown model → no costs key at all. Hmm. Which behavior do I want?

Think: pricing loaded + active, but this tick's ledger has no priced rows → header shows "Σ$0.00 · 14d"? Or nothing? My test said `assert.notOk('costs' in st, 'nothing priced → no Σ$ rollup at all')`. But wait — the global Σ$ is over the WHOLE ledger with a 14d window... if no rows priced, Σ$ genuinely is 0 for priced models. Hmm, but publishing `costs: {usd14d: 0, pricedLegs: 0}` means the header pill renders "Σ$0.00 · 14d" — which says "pricing live, zero priced spend". vs absent = "pricing off". 

Which is better? For the board: hiding when nothing priced avoids a confusing "$0.00" on factories where the pricing table exists but models don't match (e.g. pre-fa#1460 — models all empty → nothing priced → don't show $0.00). That's actually important: pre-fa#1460, ALL rows have model:null → pricedLegs 0 → showing "Σ$0.00" would be misleading ("everything free?"). So: publish `costs` only when pricedLegs > 0. That's what my test demands and it's the right call. Implementation: in buildFactoryState, `if (costs && costs.pricedLegs > 0) state.costs = costs;` — or in priceTokens return null when pricedLegs===0? No — keep priceTokens returning the summary (pure), gate at the snapshot attach. Hmm — but the "Σ$ rounds to cents" test expects usd14d=0.18 > 0 fine. And "undated rows" test: `st.costs.usd14d` = 0 with pricedLegs 0 — WAIT that test does `assert.equal(st.costs.usd14d, 0)` — it EXPECTS st.costs to exist with usd14d 0! Conflict!

Let me re-read my undated test:
```js
test('undated rows still price per-row but stay out of the Σ$ window (honest unknown)', ...
    assert.equal(cardFor(st, 31).tokens[0].cost, 3);
    assert.equal(st.costs.usd14d, 0);
    assert.equal(st.costs.pricedLegs, 0);
```
Here pricedLegs=0 (undated → out of window) but I expect st.costs to EXIST with usd14d=0. Hmm — inconsistent with the "unknown model → no costs" test? In the undated case the model IS known and priced — the ledger HAS priced spend, it's just not placeable in the window. So showing "Σ$0.00 · 14d · 0 priced legs" would... hmm. Actually what should the header show there? The rows are priced ($3 per row visible on cards) but the 14d rollup can't count them (no dates) → header Σ$ = 0.00. Is showing "Σ$0.00" while a card shows "$3.00" contradictory? A tooltip could explain... This is getting too subtle. Let me simplify to a coherent rule:

**Rule: the snapshot carries `costs` iff pricing is loaded AND at least one row priced (cost attached).** usd14d = Σ in-window; pricedLegs = rows priced in-window.

- unknown model only → no rows priced → no costs. ✔ (test 2)
- absent model only → no costs. ✔ (test 3)
- undated rows priced → rows priced (>0) → costs EXISTS, usd14d=0, pricedLegs=0. ✔ (test 4 — header shows $0.00; per-row $ shows on cards; acceptable, honest: the rollup window can't place them)

Hmm wait, but is that inconsistent-looking? pricedLegs means "in-window priced legs" — undated priced rows aren't counted. The header tooltip says "N priced legs (14d)". It's coherent: the costs block is the 14d-window rollup; its zeros mean "nothing in the window". The GATE for showing the block is "pricing produced at least one $ anywhere" — i.e., pricing is live and matching. OK.

So implementation: `if (costs && (costs.pricedLegs > 0 || ...))` — hmm, undated case: pricedLegs=0 but a row HAS cost. Gate should be "any row priced". Let me track that separately: `summary.priced = true` when any row gets cost? Or count total priced rows regardless of window: add `pricedRows` (all) vs `pricedLegs` (in-window)? Simpler: gate on "any cost attached" via a private flag. Hmm — but flag in summary leaks to snapshot. Use a local var in priceTokens:

```js
var any = false;
... row.cost = cost; any = true;
...
if (!any) return null;
return summary;
```
Wait — but then priceTokens returns null when no rows priced — and buildFactoryState `if (costs) state.costs = costs` suffices. And the undated test: any=true → costs exists, usd14d 0, pricedLegs 0 ✔. Unknown-model test: any=false → null → no costs ✔. Clean. And priceTokens pure semantics: null = "nothing priced".

3. `multi-key ledger` test failure — let me see the actual message. It failed at line `assert.notOk('cost' in cardFor(st, 31).tokens[1], 'stale row keeps model, drops cost? NO...')` — my own test comment is confusing; I wrote the assertion then contradicted it in the message and then asserted cost===3. That first notOk is WRONG (per-row cost stays regardless of window — that's my design). Remove that stray assertion (it was leftover thinking). The next line asserts equality 3 — correct behavior. Fix the test.

Wait, let me recheck what the failure message was — "expected falsy, got: true" for absent-model test = 'cost' in row is true?? For the ABSENT model test: `assert.notOk('cost' in cardFor(st, 31).tokens[0])` got true — cost attached to a model-less row?! Why? ratesFor(pricing, null)... let me re-check ratesFor:

```js
function ratesFor(pricing, model) {
    if (!pricing || model == null || model === '') return null;
```
model null → return null. priceTokens: `if (!row || row.model == null) return;` — skips before ratesFor. So cost shouldn't attach... unless the failure is from a DIFFERENT assertion in that test. The message "expected falsy, got: true" — could be `assert.notOk('costs' in st)` → 'costs' in st is true — because priceTokens returns a summary whenever pricing is set (the bug identified above, failure mode #2). Yes! Same root cause. OK.

So fixes:
- Test: `__proto__` test → build via JSON.parse.
- Test: multi-key → drop the stray notOk line.
- Impl: priceTokens returns null when no row was priced (gate via `any`).

Let me apply.

In the test I wrote the literal `{ '__proto__': {...} }` — in JavaScript, `{'__proto__': x}` in an object LITERAL sets the prototype, NOT a data property! So `Object.keys(parsed)` doesn't include '__proto__' — the parsed object has prototype {input, output} and no own keys. So `n=0`, defaultRates null → returns null. To create a real own '__proto__' data key you'd need `Object.defineProperty` or JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {...}}') — JSON.parse DOES create own property '__proto__'. So the untrusted-input path is JSON.parse — exactly the realistic path. Fix the TEST to use JSON.parse (realistic), which creates the own key.

Interesting failures:

1. `__proto__ as a model id` — `parseModelPricing({ '__proto__': {input:1, output:2} })` returned null. Why? In the test I wrote the literal `{ '__proto__': {...} }` — in JavaScript, `{'__proto__': x}` in an object LITERAL sets the prototype, NOT a data property! So `Object.keys(parsed)` doesn't include '__proto__' — the parsed object has prototype {input, output} and no own keys. So `n=0`, defaultRates null → returns null. Hmm — so my test expectation is wrong for the LITERAL case: `{'__proto__': {...}}` as a literal is a prototype assignment. To create a real own '__proto__' data key you'd need `Object.defineProperty` or JSON.parse('{"__proto__": {...}}') — JSON.parse DOES create own property '__proto__'. So the untrusted-input path is JSON.parse — exactly the realistic path. Fix the TEST to use JSON.parse (realistic), which creates the own key.

But ALSO — my implementation must handle it: with JSON.parse, `Object.keys(parsed)` includes '__proto__' (own property). `rates[k] = e` on Object.create(null) — assignment of '__proto__' key on a prototype-less object creates an own data property. Good. But wait — does GraalJS handle `obj['__proto__'] = value` on a null-prototype object as a data property? Yes — no Object.prototype.__proto__ setter inherited. Good.

Let me fix the test to use JSON.parse.

2. `unknown model → model kept, cost omitted` — "nothing priced → no Σ$ rollup at all" failed: `st.costs` exists?! Why? priceTokens returns summary whenever `pricing` is set — even when NOTHING was priced (usd14d=0, pricedLegs=0). My test expects: unknown model → no costs key at all. Hmm. Which behavior do I want?

Think: pricing loaded + active, but this tick's ledger has no priced rows → header shows "Σ$0.00 · 14d"? Or nothing? My test said `assert.notOk('costs' in st, 'nothing priced → no Σ$ rollup at all')`. But wait — the global Σ$ is over the WHOLE ledger with a 14d window... if no rows priced, Σ$ genuinely is 0 for priced models. Hmm, but publishing `costs: {usd14d: 0, pricedLegs: 0}` means the header pill renders "Σ$0.00 · 14d" — which says "pricing live, zero priced spend". vs absent = "pricing off". 

Which is better? For the board: hiding when nothing priced avoids a confusing "$0.00" on factories where the pricing table exists but models don't match (e.g. pre-fa#1460 — models all empty → nothing priced → don't show $0.00). That's actually important: pre-fa#1460, ALL rows have model:null → pricedLegs 0 → showing "Σ$0.00" would be misleading ("everything free?"). So: publish `costs` only when pricedLegs > 0. That's what my test demands and it's the right call. **Rule: the snapshot carries `costs` iff pricing is loaded AND at least one row priced (cost attached).** usd14d = Σ in-window; pricedLegs = rows priced in-window.

Hmm wait, but is that inconsistent-looking? pricedLegs means "in-window priced legs" — undated priced rows aren't counted. The header tooltip says "N priced legs (14d)". It's coherent: the costs block is the 14d-window rollup; its zeros mean "nothing in the window". The GATE for showing the block is "pricing produced at least one $ anywhere" — i.e., pricing is live and matching. OK.
